name: Keyboard Lock
plain: Lets a fullscreen page capture shortcut keys like Esc, Alt+Tab or Ctrl+W (Chromium only).
meaning: A site can keep keys the browser or OS would normally take, which remote desktops, games and cloud IDEs need. It also lets a hostile fullscreen page swallow the usual escape shortcuts for a moment.

access.prompt_ui: No prompt (needs a click, tap or keypress)
access.persistence: Ends on unlock(), leaving fullscreen or navigation; nothing is stored
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Needs the frame to be fullscreen, so cross-origin iframes need allow="fullscreen"
steps: Page calls navigator.keyboard.lock() with a list of key codes
Chosen keys go to the page instead of the browser

limits.headline: Can capture shortcut keys like Esc or Ctrl+W, but only in fullscreen on Chromium
limits.user_action: You tap Fullscreen in a game, remote desktop or web editor.
can: Capture chosen shortcut keys so a game or remote desktop receives them
Release them when you leave fullscreen
cannot: Start without a click, tap or keypress
Block system shortcuts the computer keeps for itself
Stop you leaving fullscreen, since holding Esc for about two seconds still exits
Keep capturing after you leave fullscreen
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge on computers only. Firefox and Safari do not support it.

story.what_it_is: Lets a full screen page capture shortcut keys like Esc, Alt+Tab or Ctrl+W (Chromium only).

marketing.name: Keyboard API
marketing.pitch: Explains how a page can lock keys such as Esc and system shortcuts while in full screen.

story.for_you: In full screen, keys like Esc and Alt+Tab may go to the page instead of your computer. A hint tells you to hold Esc to leave.
story.for_makers: It makes cloud gaming and remote desktops feel like the real thing, because every key reaches the game or the far computer. Sites must be in full screen first.

use_cases.example: A cloud gaming site sends every key to the game, including Windows and Esc, so menus and chat work.
A remote desktop in the browser passes Ctrl+W and Alt+Tab to the far computer instead of closing your tab.
A browser shooter keeps Esc for its own pause menu rather than letting the browser grab it.
A coding class sandbox keeps shortcuts inside the editor so students do not close the tab by mistake.
An exam site locks keys to block tab switching, which students and critics find invasive.
A music or video editor in full screen uses every key for its own shortcuts.

technical_bounds: Chrome and Edge only (no Firefox, no Safari, no iOS)
Works only while the page is fullscreen in Chrome; locking Escape means the person must hold Esc for about 2 s to leave fullscreen
Keys are named by physical KeyboardEvent.code values, not characters
Some combinations stay with the OS or browser, such as Ctrl+Alt+Del and system shortcuts like the macOS app switcher
Cannot lock keys while the tab is in the background

abuse: Trapping the person in a fullscreen spoof that eats Esc and Ctrl+W
Hiding shortcut use from the person

history.change: Keyboard Lock API ships on desktop
